Canonicalize a tensor formed by component tensors

Source: R/tensor-can.R
canonicalize.Rd

Port of SymPy's canonicalize(). The tensor is the permutation g; the free indices come first, then the dummy indices in the order d0, -d0, d1, -d1, .... Each argument in ... describes a type of component tensor as list(base_i, gens_i, n_i, sym_i): a BSGS of its slot symmetry, the number of such tensors, and their commutation symmetry (NULL none, 0 commuting, 1 anticommuting). The algorithm first minimizes the free indices with canonical_free(), then the dummy indices with double_coset_can_rep(). riemann_bsgs is the BSGS of the Riemann tensor symmetry.

Usage

canonicalize(g, dummies, msym, ...)

Arguments

g

The permutation representing the tensor.

dummies

Integer vector of dummy indices, or a list of them, one per index type.

msym

Metric symmetry (NULL, 0 or 1), or a list of them, one per index type.

...

Tensor types, each list(base_i, gens_i, n_i, sym_i).

Value

The canonical array form (integer vector), or 0 when the tensor vanishes.

Examples

b2a <- get_symmetric_group_sgs(2, 1)
g <- Permutation(c(1, 3, 0, 5, 4, 2, 6, 7))
canonicalize(g, 0:5, 0, list(b2a[[1]], b2a[[2]], 1, 0), list(b2a[[1]], b2a[[2]], 2, 0))
#> [1] 0
canonicalize(g, 0:5, 0, list(b2a[[1]], b2a[[2]], 1, 0), list(b2a[[1]], b2a[[2]], 2, 1))
#> [1] 0 2 1 4 3 5 7 6
canonicalize(Permutation(c(0, 2, 3, 1, 4, 5)), 2:3, 0,
             list(riemann_bsgs[[1]], riemann_bsgs[[2]], 1, 0))
#> [1] 0 2 1 3 5 4
